# 1. Setup

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(tidyr)
library(pROC)
library(knitr)
set.seed(1213)
```

# 2. Load data

```{r load-data}
macro <- read_csv("../data/processed/fred_md_macro_clean_final.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
macro_fin <- read_csv("../data/processed/fred_md_macro_financial_clean_final.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# data cleaning 
macro <- macro %>% mutate(sasdate = as.Date(sasdate)) %>% arrange(sasdate)
macro_fin <- macro_fin %>% mutate(sasdate = as.Date(sasdate)) %>% arrange(sasdate)

# data check if all columns present and no duplicates present
stopifnot(all(c("sasdate", "USREC") %in% names(macro)),
          all(c("sasdate", "USREC") %in% names(macro_fin)),
          !anyDuplicated(macro$sasdate), !anyDuplicated(macro_fin$sasdate))

# check dataset
kable(data.frame(dataset = c("Macro", "Macro_Financial"),
                 rows = c(nrow(macro), nrow(macro_fin)),
                 columns = c(ncol(macro), ncol(macro_fin))))
```

# 3. Construct targets 

For horizon `h`, `Y_h` equals 1 if any of the following `h` months is classified as a recession by the NBER chronology. Otherwise it equals 0. This is within-horizon forecasting, not the probability of a recession precisely at month `t+h`.

```{r targets}


create_targets <- function(df, horizons = c(3, 6, 12)) {
  df <- arrange(df, sasdate)
  for (h in horizons) {
    y <- rep(NA_integer_, nrow(df))
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(df))) {
      if (i + h <= nrow(df)) {
        future <- df$USREC[(i + 1):(i + h)]
        if (!anyNA(future)) y[i] <- as.integer(any(future == 1))
      }
    }
    df[[paste0("Y_", h)]] <- y
  }
  df
}

# whether a recession starts or occurs at any point in the next h months, not whether month t+h itself is a recessiion
macro <- create_targets(macro)
macro_fin <- create_targets(macro_fin)

macro %>%
  filter(sasdate >= as.Date("2007-01-01"), sasdate <= as.Date("2008-06-01")) %>%
  select(sasdate, USREC, Y_3, Y_6, Y_12) %>% kable()
```

# 4. Forecast design and diagnostics

The first out-of-sample forecast is January 1986. Each forecast is re-estimated on an expanding window. At forecast origin `t`, we only use training rows whose entire future target window ends before `t`. Set `announcement_delay_months` to 18 for a conservative label-availability sensitivity analysis. Zero is the directly comparable baseline. This does not fix delays in the release or revision of predictors.

```{r design}

test_start <- as.Date("1986-01-01")
horizons <- c(3, 6, 12)
announcement_delay_months <- 0L
# exclude non predictor columns
excluded <- c("sasdate", "USREC", "Y_3", "Y_6", "Y_12", "sample")

datasets <- list(Macro = macro, Macro_Financial = macro_fin)

# predictor dataset check
predictor_summary <- bind_rows(lapply(names(datasets), function(nm) {
  df <- datasets[[nm]]
  xcols <- setdiff(names(df), excluded)
  data.frame(dataset = nm, predictors = length(xcols),
             missing_predictor_cells = sum(is.na(df[, xcols, drop = FALSE])),
             recession_months = sum(df$USREC == 1, na.rm = TRUE))
}))
kable(predictor_summary)
```

# 5. Static binary response models

```{r fit-functions}

get_predictors <- function(df) {
  setdiff(names(df), excluded)
}

fit_binary <- function(train_data, predictor_cols, horizon, model = c("Logit", "Probit")) {
  model <- match.arg(model)
  target <- paste0("Y_", horizon)

  # keep only rows with a complete target and complete predictors
  train_data <- train_data[complete.cases(train_data[, c(target, predictor_cols), drop = FALSE]), , drop = FALSE]

  
  # return NULL if there are fewer than 50 usable rows, if the target has only one class (no recessions yet in training) or if there are no predictors
  if (nrow(train_data) < 50 || length(unique(train_data[[target]])) < 2L)
    return(NULL)
  if (length(predictor_cols) == 0L) return(NULL)

  # check numeric
  x <- as.matrix(train_data[, predictor_cols, drop = FALSE])
  if (!all(vapply(train_data[, predictor_cols, drop = FALSE], is.numeric, logical(1))))
    stop("Predictors must be numeric")

  # reject if more parameters than observations or if perfectly collinear
  # adds an intercept column to form the design matrix
  design <- cbind(`(Intercept)` = 1, x)
  if (ncol(design) >= nrow(design) || qr(design)$rank < ncol(design)) return(NULL)

  link <- if (model == "Logit") "logit" else "probit"
  formula <- reformulate(predictor_cols, response = target)

  # fits the unpenalised maximum-likelihood GLM, allowing up to 100 iterations
  fitted <- tryCatch(
    suppressWarnings(glm(formula, data = train_data,
                         family = binomial(link = link),
                         control = glm.control(maxit = 100))),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )

  # rejects the fit if the fit failed, did not converge or has NA or infinite coefficients, else it returns the fitted model
  if (is.null(fitted) || !isTRUE(fitted$converged) ||
      anyNA(coef(fitted)) || any(!is.finite(coef(fitted)))) return(NULL)

  fitted
}
```

# 6. Expanding-window out-of-sample forecasts

Each test observation is predicted using contemporaneous indicators and only historically eligible training labels. We drop missing predictor rows rather than imputing with future information. The same test dates must be used for model comparisons so we use paired-date checks.

```{r forecast-function}

# sets up the target and predictors
forecast_binary <- function(df, horizon, model,
                            test_start = as.Date("1986-01-01"),
                            announcement_delay_months = 0L) {
  df <- arrange(df, sasdate)
  target <- paste0("Y_", horizon)
  predictors <- get_predictors(df)
  test_idx <- which(df$sasdate >= test_start & !is.na(df[[target]]))
  output <- vector("list", length(test_idx))
  # Llops over each test date i
  for (j in seq_along(test_idx)) {
    i <- test_idx[j]
    # training outcome must be observed before forecast origin
    # monthly rows, i - h - 1 is the last strictly prior completed label
    end_idx <- i - horizon - 1L - announcement_delay_months
    prob <- NA_real_
    # olnly proceeds if there is some training data and the predictors at the test date are all observed, then takes expanding window and fits the model
    if (end_idx >= 1L &&
        all(complete.cases(df[i, predictors, drop = FALSE]))) {
      train <- df[seq_len(end_idx), , drop = FALSE]
      fit <- fit_binary(train, predictors, horizon, model)
      if (!is.null(fit)) {
        prob <- tryCatch(
          as.numeric(predict(fit, newdata = df[i, , drop = FALSE],
                             type = "response")),
          error = function(e) NA_real_
        )
        if (length(prob) != 1L || !is.finite(prob)) prob <- NA_real_
      }
    }
    output[[j]] <- data.frame(sasdate = df$sasdate[i], horizon = horizon,
                              model = model, actual = df[[target]][i],
                              predicted_prob = prob)
  }
  bind_rows(output)
}
```


Note: cache=TRUE in the chunk header means knitr skips re-running this chunk below unless the code changes.

```{r run-forecasts, cache=TRUE}

# run all at once (takes 15-20 mins)
all_forecasts <- list()
for (dataset_name in names(datasets)) {
  for (h in horizons) {
    for (model_name in c("Logit", "Probit")) {
      cat("Running:", dataset_name, h, model_name, "\n")
      result <- forecast_binary(datasets[[dataset_name]], h, model_name,
                                test_start, announcement_delay_months)
      result$dataset <- dataset_name
      all_forecasts[[paste(dataset_name, h, model_name, sep = "_")]] <- result
    }
  }
}
forecast_results <- bind_rows(all_forecasts)

forecast_results %>% group_by(dataset, horizon, model) %>%
  summarise(test_rows = n(), valid_forecasts = sum(is.finite(predicted_prob)),
            failed_forecasts = sum(!is.finite(predicted_prob)), .groups = "drop") %>% kable()
```

# 7. Out-of-sample evaluation

AUC evaluates ranking performance; F1 evaluates binary classification at the pre-specified threshold of 0.5; balanced accuracy and Brier score provide complementary diagnostics. If either class is absent or no valid forecasts exist, the affected metric is `NA`.

```{r evaluation-functions}

# keep only valid forecasts
evaluate_forecasts <- function(df, threshold = 0.5) {
  df <- df %>% filter(is.finite(predicted_prob), !is.na(actual))
  if (nrow(df) == 0) return(data.frame(n = 0L, AUC = NA_real_, F1 = NA_real_,
                                       Balanced_Accuracy = NA_real_, Brier = NA_real_))
  actual <- df$actual
  prob <- df$predicted_prob
  pred <- as.integer(prob >= threshold)
  
  # convert to to 0/1 class predictions using the 0.5 cutoff.
  tp <- sum(pred == 1 & actual == 1)
  tn <- sum(pred == 0 & actual == 0)
  fp <- sum(pred == 1 & actual == 0)
  fn <- sum(pred == 0 & actual == 1)
  
  
  # confusion matrix calculations for eval
  # Precision is the share of predicted recessions that were real (set to 0 if the model never predicted a recession)
  # Recall (sensitivity) is the share of real recession-window months caught () NA if there are no positives)
  # Specificity is the share of non-recession months correctly identified
  
  precision <- if (tp + fp == 0) 0 else tp / (tp + fp)
  recall <- if (tp + fn == 0) NA_real_ else tp / (tp + fn)
  specificity <- if (tn + fp == 0) NA_real_ else tn / (tn + fp)
  
  # F1 is the harmonic mean of precision and recall
  f1 <- if (is.na(recall)) NA_real_ else if (precision + recall == 0) 0 else
    2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall)
  
  # AUC measures how well probabilities rank recession months above non-recession months (NA if only one class is present. direction = "<" says that higher probabilities mean the positive class.)
  
  
  auc_val <- if (length(unique(actual)) < 2) NA_real_ else
    as.numeric(pROC::auc(pROC::roc(actual, prob, quiet = TRUE, direction = "<")))
  data.frame(n = nrow(df), AUC = auc_val, F1 = f1,
             Balanced_Accuracy = (recall + specificity) / 2,
             Brier = mean((actual - prob)^2))
}

evaluation_results <- forecast_results %>%
  group_by(dataset, horizon, model) %>%
  group_modify(~ evaluate_forecasts(.x)) %>% ungroup()
kable(evaluation_results, digits = 4)
```

# 8. Incremental financial-market predictive value

Compare Macro and Macro + Financial on paired valid forecast dates, not different subsamples. Positive AUC/F1 gains and positive Brier improvement indicate benefits from financial indicators.

```{r paired-comparison}
paired_forecasts <- forecast_results %>%
  select(sasdate, horizon, model, dataset, actual, predicted_prob) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = dataset,
              values_from = c(actual, predicted_prob)) %>%
  filter(is.finite(predicted_prob_Macro),
         is.finite(predicted_prob_Macro_Financial)) %>%
  mutate(actual = actual_Macro) %>%
  filter(actual_Macro == actual_Macro_Financial)


# single actual column and checks that both datasets agree on the outcome
# for AUC, F1 and balanced accuracy, a positive value means financial variables help
# Brier difference is reversed (Macro minus Financial) because lower Brier is better, so a positive value also means financial variables help.

paired_metrics <- paired_forecasts %>%
  group_by(horizon, model) %>%
  group_modify(~ {
    macro_eval <- evaluate_forecasts(data.frame(actual = .x$actual,
                                                predicted_prob = .x$predicted_prob_Macro))
    fin_eval <- evaluate_forecasts(data.frame(actual = .x$actual,
                                              predicted_prob = .x$predicted_prob_Macro_Financial))
    data.frame(n_paired = nrow(.x),
               AUC_gain = fin_eval$AUC - macro_eval$AUC,
               F1_gain = fin_eval$F1 - macro_eval$F1,
               Balanced_Accuracy_gain = fin_eval$Balanced_Accuracy - macro_eval$Balanced_Accuracy,
               Brier_improvement = macro_eval$Brier - fin_eval$Brier)
  }) %>% ungroup()
kable(paired_metrics, digits = 4)
```

# 9. Statistical significance of AUC gains: block bootstrap

The AUC gain from adding financial indicators is a single number from a test sample with only four recession episodes, so we test whether it is distinguishable from zero. We use the same paired moving-block bootstrap as the LASSO and Random Forest notebooks (24-month blocks, 1,000 resamples, seed 1213), so the results are comparable across all four models.



```{r auc-bootstrap}
block_bootstrap_auc_gain <- function(actual, prob_macro, prob_fin,
                                     block_length = 24, n_boot = 1000) {
  n <- length(actual)
  n_blocks <- ceiling(n / block_length)

  calculate_auc <- function(y, p) {
    if (length(unique(y)) < 2) return(NA_real_)
    as.numeric(pROC::auc(pROC::roc(y, p, levels = c(0, 1),
                                   direction = "<", quiet = TRUE)))
  }

  # observed improvement in AUC
  observed_gain <- calculate_auc(actual, prob_fin) - calculate_auc(actual, prob_macro)

  # bootstrap resampling of 24-month blocks (same months for both specifications)
  gains <- replicate(n_boot, {
    starts <- sample(seq_len(n - block_length + 1), n_blocks, replace = TRUE)
    idx <- unlist(lapply(starts, function(s) s:(s + block_length - 1)))[seq_len(n)]
    calculate_auc(actual[idx], prob_fin[idx]) -
      calculate_auc(actual[idx], prob_macro[idx])
  })
  gains <- gains[is.finite(gains)]
  if (length(gains) < 100) stop("Too few valid bootstrap samples.")

  data.frame(n = n,
             AUC_gain = observed_gain,
             CI_lower = unname(quantile(gains, 0.025)),
             CI_upper = unname(quantile(gains, 0.975)),
             valid_resamples = length(gains))
}

# paired_forecasts (Section 8) already keeps only dates where both specifications have valid forecasts
set.seed(1213)
auc_gain_ci <- paired_forecasts %>%
  arrange(horizon, model, sasdate) %>%
  group_by(horizon, model) %>%
  group_modify(~ block_bootstrap_auc_gain(
    actual = .x$actual,
    prob_macro = .x$predicted_prob_Macro,
    prob_fin = .x$predicted_prob_Macro_Financial
  )) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(significant = CI_lower > 0 | CI_upper < 0) %>%
  arrange(model, horizon)

kable(auc_gain_ci, digits = 4)
```

# Extension: Probit/Logit with Selected Lagged Predictors according to Economic Intuition

This extension mirrors the LASSO extension. It asks whether adding a few lagged predictors, chosen in advance on economic grounds, improves the static models. Lags of predictors are known at the forecast origin, so this does not conflict with the exclusion of lagged recession indicators. The lag specification is identical to the LASSO extension so the two are comparable. The lags were fixed before looking at any test results. Note that the unpenalised models now have more predictors, so more early-window fits may fail. Check the failed-forecast table below.

1. Define lag specifications and add lag predictors

```{r lag-spec}
lag_spec <- list(UNRATE = c(3, 6),
                 PAYEMS = c(3, 6),
                 CPIAUCSL = c(3, 6),
                 HOUST = c(3, 6),
                 S_P_500 = c(3, 6),
                 T10YFFM = c(6, 12))

# which lagged variables exist in each dataset
data.frame(variable = names(lag_spec),
           in_macro = names(lag_spec) %in% names(macro),
           in_macro_fin = names(lag_spec) %in% names(macro_fin))

# adding lag predictors to dataset
add_selected_lags <- function(df, lag_spec) {
  df <- df %>% arrange(sasdate)
  for (variable in names(lag_spec)) {
    if (!variable %in% names(df)) {
      next
    }
    for (k in lag_spec[[variable]]) {
      new_col <- paste0(variable, "_lag", k)
      df[[new_col]] <- dplyr::lag(df[[variable]], k)
    }
  }
  df
}

# targets were already built on the full sample (Section 3), before any rows are dropped
macro_lagged <- add_selected_lags(macro, lag_spec)
macro_fin_lagged <- add_selected_lags(macro_fin, lag_spec)
```

2. Handle missing observations due to lags

```{r lag-missing}
# the first 12 months have missing lags (longest lag is 12), so drop them
lag_start <- seq(min(macro$sasdate), by = "12 months", length.out = 2)[2]

macro_lagged <- macro_lagged %>% filter(sasdate >= lag_start)
macro_fin_lagged <- macro_fin_lagged %>% filter(sasdate >= lag_start)

# remaining missing predictor cells (rows with any missing predictor are dropped by the forecasting function, not imputed)
lag_excluded <- c("sasdate", "USREC", "Y_3", "Y_6", "Y_12", "sample")
sum(is.na(macro_lagged[setdiff(names(macro_lagged), lag_excluded)]))
sum(is.na(macro_fin_lagged[setdiff(names(macro_fin_lagged), lag_excluded)]))

# number of predictors with lags
c(Macro = length(get_predictors(macro_lagged)),
  Macro_Financial = length(get_predictors(macro_fin_lagged)))
```

3. Run all 12 lagged Probit/Logit configurations

```{r run-lagged-forecasts, cache=TRUE}
# same loop as Section 6, wrapped in a function so it can be reused on the lagged datasets
run_binary_models <- function(datasets) {
  all_forecasts <- list()
  for (dataset_name in names(datasets)) {
    for (h in horizons) {
      for (model_name in c("Logit", "Probit")) {
        cat("Running:", dataset_name, h, model_name, "\n")
        result <- forecast_binary(datasets[[dataset_name]], h, model_name,
                                  test_start, announcement_delay_months)
        result$dataset <- dataset_name
        all_forecasts[[paste(dataset_name, h, model_name, sep = "_")]] <- result
      }
    }
  }
  bind_rows(all_forecasts)
}

datasets_lagged <- list(Macro = macro_lagged, Macro_Financial = macro_fin_lagged)
forecast_results_lagged <- run_binary_models(datasets_lagged)

forecast_results_lagged %>% group_by(dataset, horizon, model) %>%
  summarise(test_rows = n(), valid_forecasts = sum(is.finite(predicted_prob)),
            failed_forecasts = sum(!is.finite(predicted_prob)), .groups = "drop") %>% kable()
```

4. Macro and Macro-Financial comparison

```{r lagged-evaluation}
evaluation_results_lagged <- forecast_results_lagged %>%
  group_by(dataset, horizon, model) %>%
  group_modify(~ evaluate_forecasts(.x)) %>%
  ungroup()
kable(evaluation_results_lagged, digits = 4)

# same paired logic as Section 8, wrapped in functions so they can be reused
pair_forecasts <- function(fc) {
  fc %>%
    select(sasdate, horizon, model, dataset, actual, predicted_prob) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = dataset,
                values_from = c(actual, predicted_prob)) %>%
    filter(is.finite(predicted_prob_Macro),
           is.finite(predicted_prob_Macro_Financial)) %>%
    mutate(actual = actual_Macro) %>%
    filter(actual_Macro == actual_Macro_Financial) %>%
    arrange(horizon, model, sasdate)
}

gain_table <- function(paired) {
  paired %>%
    group_by(horizon, model) %>%
    group_modify(~ {
      macro_eval <- evaluate_forecasts(data.frame(actual = .x$actual,
                                                  predicted_prob = .x$predicted_prob_Macro))
      fin_eval <- evaluate_forecasts(data.frame(actual = .x$actual,
                                                predicted_prob = .x$predicted_prob_Macro_Financial))
      data.frame(n_paired = nrow(.x),
                 AUC_gain = fin_eval$AUC - macro_eval$AUC,
                 F1_gain = fin_eval$F1 - macro_eval$F1,
                 Balanced_Accuracy_gain = fin_eval$Balanced_Accuracy - macro_eval$Balanced_Accuracy,
                 Brier_improvement = macro_eval$Brier - fin_eval$Brier)
    }) %>% ungroup()
}

paired_forecasts_lagged <- pair_forecasts(forecast_results_lagged)
financial_comparison_lagged <- gain_table(paired_forecasts_lagged)
kable(financial_comparison_lagged, digits = 4)
```

5. Statistical significance of AUC gains through block bootstrap

```{r lagged-bootstrap}

set.seed(1213)
auc_gain_ci_lagged <- paired_forecasts_lagged %>%
  group_by(horizon, model) %>%
  group_modify(~ block_bootstrap_auc_gain(
    actual = .x$actual,
```

6. Comparison of model performance with and without the lagged predictors

```{r lag-comparison}
# match original and lagged forecasts by date, model and dataset; keep dates where both are valid
paired_lag <- forecast_results %>%
  select(sasdate, horizon, model, dataset,
         actual, prob_original = predicted_prob) %>%
  inner_join(
    forecast_results_lagged %>%
      select(sasdate, horizon, model, dataset,
             actual, prob_lagged = predicted_prob),
    by = c("sasdate", "horizon", "model", "dataset", "actual")
  ) %>%
  filter(is.finite(prob_original), is.finite(prob_lagged))

# compare performance on identical forecast dates
lag_performance <- paired_lag %>%
  group_by(dataset, horizon, model) %>%
  group_modify(~ {
    original <- evaluate_forecasts(data.frame(actual = .x$actual,
                                              predicted_prob = .x$prob_original))
    lagged <- evaluate_forecasts(data.frame(actual = .x$actual,
                                            predicted_prob = .x$prob_lagged))
    data.frame(
      n_paired = nrow(.x),
      AUC_original = original$AUC,
      AUC_lagged = lagged$AUC,
      AUC_change = lagged$AUC - original$AUC,
      Brier_original = original$Brier,
      Brier_lagged = lagged$Brier,
      Brier_improvement = original$Brier - lagged$Brier
    )
  }) %>%
  ungroup()

kable(lag_performance, digits = 4)
```
